findings.title: Allow an expired unconfirmed intent to recover after a context change
findings.trigger: PREPARE an unconsumed request, switch selected session or authority generation, and let its original confirmation TTL expire without sending CONFIRM.
findings.actual: status and confirm reject CONTEXT_CHANGED before resolving expiry; prepare rejects QUALIFICATION_INTENT_PENDING because the stored state never becomes EXPIRED. Returning to the original session with a new generation also fails. summary hides the original request ID. Actual DOM shows the new-session prepare button but every click rejects; confirm and status are disabled. Only one PREPARE frame was sent, zero CONFIRM frames.
findings.impact: An ordinary session or authority change can permanently block further qualification in this Desktop lifetime even after the unconfirmed request has expired and cannot execute. There is no exposed recovery action.
findings.requested_change: Provide a bounded recovery for a provably unconfirmed expired intent, preserving its audit identity. Either reconcile the exact original request read-only before retiring it, or safely recognize its validated expiry when no CONFIRM or uncertain private command exists. Never use this path to clear a consumed or uncertain execution, and never replay CONFIRM automatically.

findings.title: Validate the current native host before reporting current qualification authorization
findings.trigger: After a successful original STATUS, replace native discovery with a different host_instance_id/data_dir while leaving the selected session context unchanged, then call qualificationCurrent or remount the qualification component.
findings.actual: currentHost explicitly throws HOST_CHANGED, but summary and the IPC qualificationCurrent reply still return available:true, authorized:true and QUALIFIED_PURPOSE_AUTHORIZED for up to ten seconds. The actual component displays the old authorization summary; a subsequent explicit STATUS fails HOST_CHANGED while that display remains.
findings.impact: The API named current delivers affirmative authorization for the old host without validating the current native host. Subsequent CONFIRM/STATUS checks do refuse the switched host, so this finding does not claim a demonstrated unauthorized model execution.
findings.requested_change: Bind summary availability and current authorization to a fresh trusted native host/process check, or return a non-authoritative historical state when that check fails. Preserve the original intent for recovery; do not relabel the old authorization as belonging to the newly selected host.
